name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle with Atrioventricular Septal Defect, Pulmonary Stenosis, and Heterotaxy Syndrome
aliases: DORV with AVSD and Pulmonary Stenosis in Heterotaxy
Complex Congenital Heart Disease with Heterotaxy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and imaging findings

criteria.description: Both great arteries arise predominantly from the right ventricle
Presence of atrioventricular septal defect involving atrial and ventricular septa
Obstruction or narrowing of the pulmonary valve or infundibulum causing pulmonary stenosis
Abnormal arrangement of thoracoabdominal organs with isomerism or situs ambiguous
Echocardiographic evidence confirming cardiac anatomical abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of double outlet right ventricle, atrioventricular septal defect, and pulmonary stenosis confirmed by imaging, with clinical or imaging evidence of heterotaxy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and imaging studies support diagnosis; no universally accepted formal diagnostic criteria exist.

pathognomonic.notes: Central cyanosis often present from birth
searchTerms: blue skin from abnormal heart blood flow
cyanosis due to right-to-left heart shunt

pathognomonic.symptomName: Heart murmur characteristic of pulmonary stenosis and septal defects
pathognomonic.notes: Systolic ejection murmur with additional pansystolic murmur
searchTerms: heart murmur from lung valve narrowing and septal defects
pulmonary stenosis murmur with heart wall defects
murmur indicating pulmonary valve and septal issues

pathognomonic.notes: Includes situs ambiguous with abnormal spleen morphology

common.symptomName: Congestive heart failure signs in infancy
searchTerms: congestive heart failure symptoms in infancy

common.notes: Due to pulmonary blood flow abnormalities
May be related to conduction system anomalies
searchTerms: irregular heart rhythms including AV block
spleen abnormalities including no spleen or many spleens

common.notes: Due to chronic hypoxia and cardiac insufficiency

occasional.notes: Secondary to immunodeficiency from splenic anomalies

searchTerms: abdominal discomfort due to bowel twisting
pain related to abnormal gut position

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to congestive hepatopathy

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to embolic stroke
searchTerms: brain function loss due to embolism

rare.notes: Rare complication of severe pulmonary hypertension

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to chronic hypoxia
Leukocytosis in cases with infection secondary to asplenia
imaging: Echocardiography showing double outlet right ventricle and AV septal defect
Cardiac MRI or CT confirming pulmonary stenosis and great vessel anatomy
Abdominal ultrasound or CT demonstrating heterotaxy and splenic anomalies
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with laterality defects (e.g., ZIC3, CFC1)
No single causative gene; heterogeneous genetic background
other: Chest X-ray revealing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of ventricular septal defect with overriding aorta and right ventricular hypertrophy
Pulmonary stenosis but absence of atrioventricular septal defect
Similar heterotaxy features but different cardiac anatomy
AV septal defect present without double outlet right ventricle

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Recurrent severe infections due to asplenia
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2010.
Mahle WT, et al. Heterotaxy syndrome: clinical features and management. Pediatr Cardiol. 2010;31(3):351-361.
Orphanet: Double outlet right ventricle with atrioventricular septal defect, pulmonary stenosis, heterotaxy syndrome (ORPHA:423712).
